title: Run the Go platform witness, not just its cross-compiler
applies_when: A pure-Go package has OS-dependent path or filesystem behavior, the target Windows machine lacks Go, and an authorized Linux build host is available. Source and test dependencies must be independently inspected and runnable in task-private directories.
lesson: Use a pinned Go toolchain to cross-build the real package test executable with CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o fs.test.exe ./package. Bind the source revision plus test bytes, verify the transferred executable hash, then actually run it on native Windows with task-private TEMP/TMP. Compare unchanged baseline and repair using the identical regression, and retain a Linux control. Cross-compilation alone cannot expose runtime separators. A standalone test executable does not carry external testdata: use a reviewed package working directory with hash-verified fixtures. Preserve missing-fixture failures; rerun the identical binary with the correct runtime inputs rather than patching production or dropping tests. For ZIPs, assert archive entry names from a nested directory source; archiving one file may retain only its basename and miss the recursive join. Keep archive-internal path.Join separate from filesystem filepath.Join, but do not infer a defect from the import alone: afero's index and lookup both normalize with filepath, and the original issue395 archive passes on current Windows source. A focused pass does not erase an unchanged broader-suite failure: record its baseline/candidate result and test inventory separately. Inspect hosted CI commands before treating a green badge as a platform witness: Afero PR700's successful AppVeyor log only shows go version and test discovery, not a test invocation or results.
avoid_when: Do not disable cgo to pretend that a cgo-dependent production path was tested; cross-builds can exclude files and require a C cross-compiler or target libraries. Match target architecture and OS capabilities, check source and test safety before execution, and do not start local WSL or install global tools merely to reproduce this workflow. An application-control denial is unexecuted, not test failure or permission to rename/move/re-route the binary. Evidence covers a goraven Go1.27.2 repair and an afero Go1.26.9 negative witness, not full application/CI, all archives, old runtimes or universal Windows support. No claim of measured cost savings, PR acceptance, recall or throughput follows from the method.

evidence.note: Official Go guidance distinguishes cross-building pure-Go Windows executables from running them on Windows, describes initial standard-library build/cache cost, and warns that cgo inputs can be excluded. Mechanism documentation, not a measured result.
FileHeader.Name requires relative forward-slash paths. This archive format contract differs from native filesystem path separators.

Submitted source-bound Root.Zip regression: nested archive names fail on native Windows before the path.Join repair and pass after; Linux core/fs tests pass on both. The test binary was built on Linux with Go1.27.2 and executed on Windows. An existing leading-slash return-path assertion fails unchanged in the broader Windows package run and is explicitly disclosed. Publication is not maintainer acceptance or full application qualification.

Scoped owner feedback: unchanged eb6a928, Windows/amd64 Go1.26.9 CGO=0, original attached ZIP and three directory/file controls pass. Existing zipfs tests also pass after supplying their original runtime fixtures. Three first-run failures were missing testdata from the executable's working directory; the same binary succeeds with verified fixtures. Not a full root-module, race, old-version or every-archive claim.

splitpath, index construction and lookup use consistent filepath normalization. This is not writing native separators into archive FileHeader.Name; check the actual producer/consumer contract before transferring the goraven repair.

Hosted PR700 head80658d58: successful two-second Windows job logs Go1.13.3 version and test discovery, with no go test command or results. This badge does not close the disclosed Windows runtime gap; GitHub Actions separately awaits maintainer approval.
